details.description: GPT-5.2-Codex is OpenAI's coding-specialized version of GPT-5.2, released December 18, 2025 as, in OpenAI's words, "our most advanced agentic coding model yet for complex, real-world software engineering." Per OpenAI's system-card addendum, it adds long-horizon work via context compaction, stronger performance on large-scale changes such as refactors and migrations, improved behavior in Windows environments, and significantly stronger cybersecurity capabilities than prior Codex models -- rated 'very capable' in cybersecurity under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, though below the framework's High-capability threshold. It takes text and image input, produces text output, and supports four reasoning-effort levels (low, medium, high, xhigh) with a knowledge cutoff of August 31, 2025. As of this research it has already been formally retired: OpenAI's deprecations page lists a shutdown date of July 23, 2026 (already past) with gpt-5.6-sol as the replacement, and it has been superseded in Codex by GPT-5.3-Codex.
advantages: OpenAI's system-card addendum rates it 'very capable' in the cybersecurity domain under the Preparedness Framework, its strongest cybersecurity rating yet for a Codex model, though still below the framework's High-capability threshold.
Adds long-horizon agentic coding via context compaction and stronger performance on large-scale refactors and migrations than prior Codex models, per OpenAI's system-card addendum.
Scores 29 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (xhigh reasoning), ranked above average among comparable models (Artificial Analysis).
Supports low/medium/high/xhigh reasoning effort and agentic tool use -- function calling, web search, hosted shell and skills -- via OpenAI's Responses API (OpenAI API docs).
disadvantages: OpenAI's API deprecations page lists this model's shutdown date as July 23, 2026 -- already past as of this research date -- with gpt-5.6-sol as the recommended replacement.

GitHub reports it was deprecated across most GitHub Copilot experiences by June 5, 2026, with GPT-5.3-Codex recommended instead, and Artificial Analysis also lists it as deprecated with GPT-5.3-Codex (xhigh) as successor.
OpenAI treats the model as High capability on biology under its Preparedness Framework, the same safeguard tier applied across the GPT-5 family (OpenAI system-card addendum).
Output is text-only; the model does not generate images, audio or video (OpenAI API docs).
use_cases: Complex, real-world software engineering and agentic coding
Long-horizon coding tasks via context compaction
Coding work in Windows development environments
Vetted, invite-only security research and cybersecurity-related coding tasks

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens (272,000) conflicts with OpenAI's own model-card page, which states a 400,000-token context window; kept the catalog's value per instructions. Catalog lists /v1/chat/completions as a supported endpoint, but OpenAI's model-card page states only the Responses API is supported for this model and that Chat Completions, Batch, Assistants and fine-tuning are unsupported; kept the catalog's endpoint facts as instructed but flagging the conflict. Catalog's deprecation_date (2027-07-13) is about a year later than the July 23, 2026 shutdown date OpenAI's own deprecations page lists for this exact model id, which had already passed as of this research date (2026-09-24).
